# Results — Study 731 (Wimbledon-Effect)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **the
Wimbledon fortnight is the UK market's quiet "summer lull"**, a low-energy
tennis-and-strawberries window with its own tradable signature — is pure City folklore,
the British sibling of *Sell-in-May*. Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last
complete calendar month). Fingerprint `da4f039bf903` (EWU + VGK, one combined panel,
5,555 rows).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `EWU` (iShares MSCI United Kingdom) + `VGK` (Vanguard FTSE Europe), one combined panel: 5,555 rows, 2004-06-01 → 2026-06-30 |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: 21 Championships years 2005→2025 (**2020 COVID-cancelled** → 20 contested), each with its exact fortnight start (first Monday) and end (second Sunday, gentlemen's final); every non-cancelled pair asserted Monday→Sunday / 13 days at import (Wikipedia "Wimbledon Championships" + per-year pages) |
| Events resolvable | all **20** contested fortnights have EWU + VGK coverage — VGK's 2005-03-10 inception is the reason the sample starts at the 2005 Championships, not EWU's 1996 inception |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the window return across independent, non-overlapping yearly events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson up-rate interval; a 20-seed × 200-draw two-sided random-window placebo; a per-year realized-vol-ratio test; leave-one-out jackknife; a pre-2015 vs 2015+ split |
| Execution / costs | **calendar-known window → no execution lag, zero look-ahead** (dates published years ahead). Entry = last close *before* the first Monday; exit = last close on/before the second Sunday (≈10-session hold). Long-only = 2 one-way legs × NAV; market-neutral (long EWU / short VGK) = 4 legs + borrow on the short (0.50%/yr) |
| Adjustment | **total-return** (dividends reinvested, `auto_adjust=True`) for both ETFs — labelled, not price-only |

## The signal — fortnight window return (entry close → exit close)

| cut | n | mean | sd | *t* | up-rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| raw EWU | 20 | **+0.377%** | 2.794% | **+0.604** | 12/20 = 60.0% [38.7%, 78.1%] |
| abnormal (EWU − VGK) | 20 | **−0.218%** | 0.715% | **−1.360** | 8/20 = 40.0% [21.9%, 61.3%] |

Neither cut clears the desk's |*t*| ≥ 2 bar. The raw +0.377% is simply the ordinary
drift of a rising market held for two weeks; the −0.218% abnormal is a whisper of
UK-specific softness with no statistical spine.

## Random-window placebo (20 seeds × 200 draws, two-sided)

| cut | observed | placebo mean (sd) | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| raw | +0.377% | +0.265% (0.837%) | 0.670 |
| abnormal | −0.218% | −0.051% (0.269%) | 0.424 |

Both observed means sit in the fat middle of what a random two-week window on the *same
tickers* produces — a random fortnight matches or beats the raw Wimbledon return ~67% of
the time. There is nothing calendar-special about the window.

## The volatility lull — the myth's own claim, tested directly

Per-year log realized-vol ratio, fortnight vs a symmetric ±25-session neighbourhood:

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| mean log-ratio | +0.0086 |
| mean ratio | **1.009** |
| one-sample *t* | **+0.093** |
| quieter than neighbours | **10/20 = 50.0%** (Wilson [29.9%, 70.1%]) |

The fortnight's daily moves are the same size as the surrounding weeks, and it is
quieter than its neighbours in exactly half the years — a coin flip. Whatever thinning
of volume the City feels, it does **not** show up as lower realized volatility. The
literal "quiet window" claim is **busted** on its own terms.

## Robustness — jackknife and the 2015 format split

| check | result |
|---|---|
| raw, leave-one-out *t* range | **[+0.249, +1.242]** — never near 2 |
| abnormal, leave-one-out *t* range | **[−2.015, −0.981]** — grazes −2 once, then killed by the placebo (*p* = 0.42) |
| pre-2015 raw *t* (n=10) | +0.288 |
| 2015+ raw *t* (n=10) | +0.679 |
| Welch (early − late) | **−0.089** |

The 2015 schedule shift (the fortnight moved a week later) changes nothing. No single
year and no regime carries a signal, because there is no signal to carry.

## Event anatomy — mean cumulative return by session offset from entry

| session | 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| raw EWU | 0.000% | −0.602% | −0.189% | −0.067% | −0.042% | +0.318% |
| abnormal | 0.000% | +0.097% | +0.083% | −0.010% | −0.153% | −0.166% |

No shape: the raw path dips early, wanders, and recovers to roughly flat-plus by the
close; the abnormal path oscillates around zero. Nothing resembling a coherent
lull-and-release or a steady drift — just the meander of a small sample of two-week
windows.

## Tradability — the calendar-known trade, net of costs

Entered at the close before the first Monday, exited at the close inside the fortnight
(zero look-ahead, dates known years ahead).

| construction | cost | gross | net (*t*) | win rate |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| long-only EWU | 5 bps | +0.377% (*t* = +0.60) | +0.277% (+0.44) | 12/20 |
| long-only EWU | 10 bps | +0.377% | +0.177% (+0.28) | 12/20 |
| market-neutral (long EWU / short VGK) | 5 bps | −0.218% (*t* = −1.36) | **−0.436% (−2.72)** | 5/20 |
| market-neutral | 10 bps | −0.218% | −0.636% (−3.98) | 4/20 |

Two placebo checks: long-only net **p = 0.746**, market-neutral net **p = 0.272** — both
deep in the bulk.

**The one instructive trap.** The market-neutral net return is the *only* number in the
whole study that clears |*t*| ≥ 2 — and it is a **loss** of −0.436%, *t* = −2.72. It is
significant not because there is a real "short the UK for Wimbledon" edge (the **gross**
spread is *t* = −1.36, insignificant, placebo *p* = 0.42) but because a market-neutral
book pays a **deterministic ~0.218% cost + borrow drag** over the two-week hold, and
subtracting a fixed drag from a near-zero-mean distribution mechanically shoves the whole
thing below −2. The proof: **reverse** the trade (short EWU / long VGK) and it nets
**−0.001%**, *t* = **−0.00** — the mirror-image gross is eaten by the same symmetric
drag, so *no direction pays*. A careless writer could sell the −2.72 as "a significant
Wimbledon short." It is significant, and it is worthless.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic paired (asset, benchmark) log-return world (ρ ≈ 0.85, like a UK ETF vs
Europe) with a fixed synthetic fortnight window each year and a TUNABLE planted seasonal;
no network.

| world | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (seasonal = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.08** (sd 0.91), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted seasonal = +1.0% (seed 731) | **+2.41** |
| planted seasonal = +2.0% (seed 731) | **+4.23** |

The detector recovers a planted seasonal and never fires on the null — the flat
real-tape answer is the tape's, not the detector's. *(A faithful-engine / power check
only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** No directional seasonal, raw or UK-specific: raw *t* = +0.60
  (placebo *p* = 0.67), abnormal *t* = −1.36 (placebo *p* = 0.42). Both cuts sit inside
  the random-window cloud, robust to a leave-one-out jackknife and a pre/post-2015 split.
  No published academic anchor to lean on — pure folklore, and the tape agrees it is
  folklore.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Long-only net (+0.277%, *t* = +0.44, placebo *p* = 0.75) is
  just two weeks of market beta; the only |*t*| ≥ 2 number in the study (market-neutral
  net *t* = −2.72) is a **loss** generated entirely by a ~0.218% cost/borrow drag on a
  *t* = −1.36 gross spread, and the reverse trade nets −0.001%. No tradable direction
  exists.
- **"A real lull?" — BUSTED.** Realized-vol ratio 1.009 (*t* = +0.09), quieter in
  10/20 years. The fortnight is not measurably quieter than the weeks around it — the
  folklore's own core claim fails.
